results.synthesis: Zebra stripes work like a group camouflage trick, confusing predators about where one zebra ends and the next begins in a moving herd.
results.explanation: The stripes make it hard for lions to tell where one zebra stops and another starts when they're all running together.
results.headline: You nailed the twist!
results.feedbackText: Yes! You landed the exact insight that makes zebra stripes so clever: the camouflage isn't about hiding one zebra, it's about **blurring the whole herd into one confusing mass** so a lion can't lock onto a single target. The running-together part is what makes it work.

results.q: why do we get déjà vu
results.synthesis: Déjà vu is likely a brief glitch where your brain's familiarity-detection system fires before your memory-recall system catches up, so a new moment feels tagged as remembered.
results.explanation: It's your brain remembering a dream you had.
results.headline: Warm, familiar feeling!
results.feedbackText: That dream-memory idea is exactly the kind of thing déjà vu feels like, which is why so many people reach for it! The twist we landed on is that it is less about a real memory and more about a **timing glitch** where your brain's familiarity signal fires a beat before recall catches up, so a brand-new moment gets tagged as already remembered.
